description: Each patient's HGB/HCT ratio is their mean HGB divided by their mean HCT.

b.request: For each patient, divide their mean non-missing HGB by their mean non-missing HCT; among patients whose resulting ratio exceeds the mean of these ratios across all patients, return one row with the mean of their per-patient average PIC values, the mean of their ratios, and the mean amount their ratios exceed the cross-patient mean
b.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.HGB) AS avg_hgb, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct, AVG(l.PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID), patient_ratios AS (SELECT avg_pic, avg_hgb / NULLIF(avg_hct, 0) AS ratio FROM patient_averages), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM patient_ratios) SELECT AVG(pr.avg_pic) AS mean_pic, AVG(pr.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(pr.ratio - o.mean_ratio) AS mean_excess FROM patient_ratios AS pr CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE pr.ratio > o.mean_ratio;

c.request: Looking at each patient's hemoglobin-to-hematocrit (`HGB`/`HCT`) ratio from their lab records (ignoring missing values), take the patients whose ratio is above the average across all patients. Give one summary row for them: the mean of their average PIC, the mean of their ratios, and the mean amount by which their ratios exceed that cross-patient average. Each patient's HGB/HCT ratio is their mean HGB divided by their mean HCT.
c.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), cross_patient_average AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM patient_averages) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - c.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess_ratio FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN cross_patient_average AS c WHERE p.ratio > c.avg_ratio;

a.request: For each patient in the Laboratory table, compute their average PIC and their hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio, taken as their average `HGB` divided by their average `HCT` (ignoring missing values). Keep the patients whose ratio is above the average of all patients' ratios, and give one summary row for them: the average of their average PIC values, the average of their ratios, and the average amount by which their ratios exceed that all-patient average.
a.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic, AVG(HGB) / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), all_patient_average AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM patient_averages) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS average_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS average_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - a.avg_ratio) AS average_excess FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN all_patient_average AS a WHERE p.ratio > a.avg_ratio;

d.request: Using each patient’s lab records and ignoring missing values, calculate their HGB/HCT ratio as their mean HGB divided by their mean HCT. Select patients whose ratio exceeds the average ratio across all patients. For those patients, return one summary row with the mean of their per-patient average PIC, the mean of their ratios, and the mean amount by which their ratios exceed the cross-patient average.
d.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic, AVG(HGB) / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM patient_averages) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - o.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess_ratio FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o WHERE p.ratio > o.avg_ratio;
